q: When did Hazardous waste management act enacted in India?
solution: Explanation: The Ministry of Environment & Forests, Government of India, notified the Hazardous Waste (Management & Handling) Rules on July 28, 1989. This was done under the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

q: Who is responsible for safe disposal of the generated hazardous waste?
solution: Explanation: The generator is responsible for the safe disposal of waste being produced by them and also is accountable for the clean-up in case of an accident.

q: The activities of hazardous waste management facility are?
solution: Explanation: The activities of a hazardous waste management facility are defined by the acronym TSD, which stands for Treatment, Storage, and Disposal. Treatment: Changing the physical, chemical, or biological character of the waste to neutralize it or make it less hazardous. Storage: Holding the hazardous waste for a temporary period before it is treated, disposed of, or stored elsewhere. Disposal: The final placement of waste in or on the land, such as in a landfill or injection well, in an environmentally sound manner.

q: Regulations for waste management is provided under subtitle C of
solution: Explanation: Regulations for waste management are provided under subtitle C of RCRA (Resource Conservation and Recovery Act). Key Details regarding RCRA Subtitle C: Hazardous Waste Management : Subtitle C establishes a "cradle-to-grave" system for managing hazardous waste, covering it from generation to transport, treatment, storage, and disposal. Regulations: Subtitle C regulations are found in 40 CFR parts 260 through 279. Subtitle C vs. D: Subtitle C regulates hazardous waste, while Subtitle D focuses on non-hazardous solid waste.

q: Tracking of the hazardous waste is done to prevent?
solution: Explanation: Tracking of hazardous waste is done to prevent illegal dumping and abandoning of the waste which will be menace to public.

q: Why is manifest system necessary?
solution: Explanation: The manifest system helps to get rid of the problem of midnight dumping and provides means for determining the type and amount of hazardous waste being generated.

q: Under MTCA, the process for cleaning up a hazardous waste site is
solution: Explanation: Site Hazard Assessment (SHA) is the process for cleaning up a hazardous waste site under Model Toxic Control Act.

q: According to the Solid Waste Management Rules, what is the mandatory segregation requirement for waste generators?
options: Three streams: biodegradable, dry, and domestic hazardous.
Four streams: organic, paper, plastic, and metal.
solution: Under Rule 4 of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, every waste generator must segregate waste into three separate streams: Biodegradable, Non-biodegradable, and Domestic Hazardous Waste (e.g., diapers, cleaning agents, mosquito repellents) before handing it over to collectors.

q: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2024, introduce environmental compensation based on which principle?
solution: Explanation: The draft rules for 2024 explicitly state that environmental compensation will be levied on waste generators, bulk generators, and local bodies for non-compliance, implementing the "Polluter Pays Principle ".

q: Under the E-Waste (Management) Amendment Rules, 2024, the Central Government may establish a platform for trading what?
solution: Explanation: The 2024 amendment to the E-Waste rules introduces a new provision for establishing a centralized platform for the trading and exchange of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) certificates.

q: The active period of landfill range from years.
solution: As per CPHEEO Manual, A landfill design life will comprise of an ‘active’ period and an ‘closure and post-closure’ period. The ‘active’ period may typically range from 10 to25 years depending on the availability of land area. The ‘closure and post-closure’ period for which a landfill will be monitored and maintained will be 25 years after the ‘active period’ is completed.

q: At what flash point is liquid waste considered ignitable?
solution: Explanation: A liquid waste is classified as ignitable (EPA hazardous waste code D001 ) if its flash point is less than 60°C (140°F). This threshold is determined using standardized closed-cup testing methods (such as ASTM D93-79 or D93-80 ) to identify liquids that pose a fire hazard during transport, storage, or disposal.

q: Hydrological investigation has to be done for ?
solution: Explanation: Hydrological investigation has to be done for collection of hydro-meteorological data and topographical maps of surrounding area

q: Before shipment, hazardous waste has to be properly.
solution: Explanation: When preparing for a shipment, the hazardous waste has to be properly packed and contents has to be labelled .

q: How many hazard classes should be taken into account while packing the waste?
solution: Explanation: Nine hazard classes should be considered while classifying the hazardous material for packing and the hazards associated with the material should also be considered.

q: Inorganic liquid waste are best suitable in ?
solution: Explanation: Inorganic liquid wastes, such as strong acids, bases, and aqueous chemical solutions, are best suited for storage in plastic cans or polyethylene tanks. This is because: Chemical Compatibility: Plastic (specifically high-density polyethylene or HDPE) is chemically inert and does not react with corrosive inorganic substances. Durability: These containers can withstand a wide range of temperatures and provide superior leak protection. Standard Sizing: They are typically used in capacities of 30, 45, or 200 liters for industrial and laboratory waste management.

q: Hazard labels are shaped. ?
solution: Explanation: Hazard labels are diamond shaped and are required for dangerous goods except magnetized materials.

q: Labels should be at least mm square ?
solution: Explanation: Labels should be at least 100mm square . They must be legible and recognizable in the day time and at night.

q: Incineration of HW is done at TSDF to reduce?
solution: Explanation : Incineration is a thermal treatment process used at Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDF) primarily to reduce the volume and mass of the waste (often by up to 90%) and to detoxify it by destroying organic hazardous constituents.

q: An external safety audit at an incinerator facility is typically carried out once every ______ years.
solution: Explanation: As per standard industrial safety codes (such as IS 14489:1998 Code of Practice on Occupational Safety and Health Audit), an external safety audit must be conducted by a competent independent agency once every 2 years. Internal audits are usually conducted every year.

q: What type of waste does Subtitle D of RCRA regulate?
solution: Subtitle D of the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) focuses on the management of non-hazardous solid waste. It encourages states to develop comprehensive plans for the disposal and management of non-hazardous waste, such as municipal solid waste (household garbage) and non-hazardous industrial waste. Key regulatory actions under Subtitle D include: Banning Open Dumping: It prohibits the open dumping of waste and establishes technical criteria for landfills. Setting Landfill Standards: It provides minimum federal criteria for the design, operation, and location of municipal and industrial solid waste landfills. State Implementation: Unlike Subtitle C, which is primarily federal, Subtitle D gives states the lead role in implementing and enforcing these regulations.

q: Hazardous waste Permits are typically granted for a period up to _ _____years.
solution: Explanation: Permit durations vary widely, but common examples suggest periods like 4 years for public sanitation permits, 10 years for hazardous waste facilities, or even 10 years for some specific licenses, though short-term work permits might only last 24 hours , so the answer depends on the specific type of permit. Here's a breakdown: Hazardous Waste Permits : Often granted for up to 10 years for treatment, storage, and disposal facilities (TSDFs). Public Place Sanitation Permits : Generally valid for 4 years in China, with potential local variations. Amateur Radio Licenses (ASOC): Can be renewed up to 10 years in India under specific conditions. Permits to Work (PTW) : For specific tasks, these are typically short-term, often valid for only 24 hours to ensure safety checks are frequent.

q: What is the first step in development of dose-response relationship curve?
solution: Explanation: The first step in development of dose-response relationship curve is selecting toxicological end point which is caused by exposure to selected chemical.

q: The toxicological end point for dose-response relationship should be
solution: Explanation: The toxicological end point for dose-response relationship should be clear, definitive and directly measurable such as death.

q: According to the graph, greater the dose more the response.
solution: Explanation: Greater the dose, the more severe the response is i.e. greater the number of chemical-receptor complex, the more severe response.

q: The highest dose that has no harmful effect on a population is known as
solution: Explanation: NOAEL stands for No Observed Adverse Effect Level. It is defined in toxicology as the highest dose or exposure level of a substance at which there are no statistically or biologically significant increases in the frequency or severity of adverse (harmful) effects compared to a control population. While some non-harmful biological changes might still occur at this dose, they are not considered detrimental to the organism's health. It serves as a critical threshold for establishing safe exposure limits and human starting doses in clinical trials.

q: As per UNEPA in 1985, waste is considered hazardous if it?
options: Poses threat to human and environment
solution: Explanation: According to the definitions historically used by regulatory bodies like the USEPA (particularly following the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976 and subsequent 1980s regulations), a waste is considered hazardous if its properties make it dangerous or capable of having a harmful effect on human health or the environment . In 1985 specifically, the EPA refined these definitions through the "Final Codification Rule," which established that waste exhibiting certain characteristics—such as toxicity, reactivity, ignitability, or corrosivity —merits regulation because it poses a sufficient threat.

q: According to EPA hazardous mixed waste is regulated under?
solution: Explanation: Mixed wastes are hazardous waste that contain radioactive materials, according to EPA HW in mixed waste is regulated under RCRA and Atomic Energy Act.

q: Under Schedule II of the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, Class C2 focuses on which characteristic?
solution: Explanation: According to Schedule II (Part C) of the Hazardous Waste Management Rules, 2016, the hazard classes are: Class C1: Flammability Class C2: Corrosivity Class C3: Reactivity or Explosivity Class C4: Toxicity Class C5: Substances that act on other materials (Carcinogenicity/Mutagenicity)

q: What is the maximum concentration limit (in mg/L) for the Class A1 element according to Schedule II of the Hazardous Waste Management Rules?
solution: Explanation: Element Identification: The A1 element listed under Class A of Schedule II is Arsenic. Concentration Limit: The regulatory limit for this substance is established at 5.0 mg/L. Note on Schedule II Under the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules , Schedule II categorizes waste based on the concentration of specific constituents. Class A substances are those where the concentration limit is typically measured in milligrams per liter (mg/L) or milligrams per kilogram (mg/kg) to determine if the waste is hazardous.

q: When did the Toxic Substances Control Act came into force?
solution: Explanation: The Toxic Substances Control Act came into force on 1976. It provides EPA with authority to necessitate reporting, keeping records and restrictions relating to chemical substances.

q: What is the purpose of TSCA compliance monitoring program?
solution: Correct Answer (a): Explanation: EPA and the States verify TSCA agreement through a complete TSCA compliance monitoring program which includes inspecting the facilities, revising records and taking enforcement action where necessary for pollution prevention.

q: _______ plays a major role in the regulation of most industrial chemicals in the US.
solution: Correct Answer (d): Explanation: Section 8 of TSCA requires EPA to compile, keep current records and publish a list of chemical substance that is being manufactured, Including imports, in the US for uses under TSCA inventory.

q: Any chemical that is not on the Inventory is considered as ________
solution: Correct Answer (a): Explanation: According to regulations under TSCA, if a chemical is on the Inventory, it is considered an existing chemical substance in United States commerce. Any chemical that is not on the Inventory is considered a new chemical substance.

q: The chemicals are added to the Inventory only after?
solution: Explanation: Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA), a company must submit a Notice of Commencement of Manufacture or Import (NOC) to the EPA within 30 calendar days of the substance first being manufactured or imported. Once the EPA receives a complete and valid NOC, the reported substance is officially added to the TSCA Inventory

q: EPA's collecting of the public TSCA Inventory information is updated a year.
solution: Answer: b Explanation: TSCA Inventory information is updated twice a year to include new and corrected TSCA Inventory chemical listings. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) updates and releases the public TSCA Inventory biannually, not annually. This non-confidential Inventory information is released twice a year as part of its routine data dissemination. Key Details Frequency:The public TSCA Inventory is updated and released twice a year. Purpose:This update allows for the dissemination of non-confidential TSCA Inventory data

q: 11. What is the aim of TSCA?
solution: Answer: a Explanation: TSCA is a United States law signed on October 11, 1976 which regulates the introduction of new or already existing chemicals.

q: The program for the cleanup of closed or abandoned hazardous waste sites is administered by EPA .
solution: Answer: a Explanation : The Superfund program for the cleanup of closed or abandoned hazardous waste sites is administered by EPA under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA).

q: Which policy offers a national framework for waste management and resource recovery in Australia?
solution: The National waste policy (specifically the 2018 policy and the 2019 Action Plan) provides the comprehensive national framework for waste management and resource recovery in Australia. It is designed to guide collective action from governments, businesses, and communities to improve recycling and manage materials more sustainably by 2030. Key Objectives and Targets: Waste Reduction: Achieving a 10% reduction in waste generated per person. Recovery Rate: Reaching an 80% average resource recovery rate from all waste streams. Recycled Content: Significantly increasing the use of recycled content by 2030. Core Principles: The policy focuses on avoiding waste, improving resource recovery, and managing material flows effectively.

q: Which act is responsible for reducing pollution at source?
solution: Answer: c Explanation: Pollution prevention is reducing waste at source by modifying production processes, encouraging the use of nontoxic substances, implementing resource conservation techniques, and reusing materials.

q: _______ law covers the discharge of waste into environment in NY.
solution: Answer: a Explanation: The Hazardous Waste Reduction Plan ( HWRP ) accounts for hazardous wastes which emitted into air, discharged into waters, or treated and disposed of in a facility.

q: Which of the following HW cannot be recycled?
solution: Explanation: Treatment waste (also referred to as residues from hazardous waste treatment processes) often cannot be recycled because it represents the final byproduct of hazardous waste neutralization or stabilization. These residues are typically highly concentrated or chemically stable inert materials meant for final disposal in secured landfills rather than further recovery. While the other materials listed are considered hazardous, they have well-established recycling streams: Used oil: Can be re-refined into new motor oil or processed into fuel oils. Paints: Leftover latex and oil-based paints are frequently collected for bulk recycling where they are reprocessed into new paint products. Batteries: Lead-acid and various household batteries (like nickel-cadmium or lithium-ion) contain valuable metals that are recovered through specialized recycling processes.

q: Which of the following techniques can be implemented to reduce hazardous waste?
solution: Answer: d Explanation: By notifying materials handler, the excess chemicals can be used by someone else .

q: Which approach should be considered to reduce the impact of waste on the environment?
options: CERCLA (Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act)
solution: Explanation: By employing Life Cycle Analysis (LCA) methods, corporations and agencies can identify specific opportunities to reduce environmental impacts throughout the entire lifespan of a product or process.

q: When was The National Environmental Policy Act was signed into law?
solution: Explanation: The National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) was signed into law on January 1, 1970. NEPA entails federal agencies to evaluate the environmental effects of proposed actions former to making decisions and to suggest alternatives.

q: What do Section 102 in Title I of the NEPA Act requires?
solution: Answer: b Explanation: Section 102 in Title I of the Act requires federal agencies to incorporate environmental considerations in their planning and decision - making through a systematic interdisciplinary approach.

q: The National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) is ________environmental law.
solution: Answer: a Explanation: he National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) is a United States environmental law enacted on 1 January 1970 promotes the enhancement of the environment and also established the President's Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ).

q: What are three levels of analysis that a federal agency must undertake to comply with the law NEPA?
solution: Explanation: The National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) requires federal agencies to assess environmental effects using three primary levels of analysis: 1. Categorical Exclusion (CatEx): For actions that do not individually or cumulatively have a significant environmental effect. 2. Environmental Assessment (EA): Determines if the project has the potential to cause significant environmental effects. 3. Environmental Impact Statement (EIS): The most rigorous level of analysis, required if the action will significantly affect the quality of the human environment.

q: Safety and Health Achievement Recognition Program (SHARP) recognizes
options: Small employers who operate safety and health management system
Large employers who operate safety and health management system
All employers who operate safety and health management system
Workers who operate safety and health management system
solution: Answer: a Explanation: Employers who are accepted into SHARP are accepted as models for worksite safety and health. Upon receiving SHARP recognition, the worksite will be excused from programmed inspections during the period that the SHARP certification is valid.

q: In 2016, the EPA announced final updates to its New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) to reduce emissions of which type of landfill gas?
solution: Explanation: On August 29, 2016, the EPA announced final updates to the New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) specifically designed to reduce emissions of methane-rich landfill gas from new, modified, and reconstructed municipal solid waste (MSW) landfills. Key Details of the 2016 Update: Pollutant Focus: The standards chiefly target methane, which is a potent greenhouse gas. Impact: The combined rules were estimated to reduce methane emissions by approximately 334,000 metric tons by 2025. Lowered Threshold: The update lowered the emission threshold for when landfills must install gas collection and control systems from 50 metric tons of non-methane organic compounds (NMOC) per year to 34 metric tons. Regulatory Structure: To implement these changes, the EPA established a new subpart (Subpart XXX) for facilities built or modified after July 17, 2014.

q: In the context of the transport of hazardous waste, what does "TREM Card" stand for?
solution: TREM Card stands for Transport Emergency Card . It is a mandatory document that must accompany the driver during the transportation of hazardous goods. It contains critical safety information, such as the nature of the hazard, protective devices required, and emergency actions to be taken in case of an accident or spillage (e.g., fire, explosion, or leakage) to minimize environmental and health damage.

q: As per the Hazardous Waste Management Rules, 2016, a waste generator can store hazardous waste for a maximum period of:
solution: According to Rule 8 of the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 , the occupiers (waste generators) may store hazardous and other wastes for a period not exceeding 90 days . Note: This period can be extended by the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) in specific cases (e.g., small generators), but 90 days is the standard statutory limit.

q: The "Manifest System" for the movement of hazardous waste within the country requires how many copies (color-coded) to be generated?
solution: The manifest system tracks hazardous waste from "cradle to grave" (generation to disposal). Under the Hazardous Waste Management Rules, 2016 (Form 10) , the sender must prepare 7 copies of the manifest. These copies are color-coded and distributed among the Sender, Transporter, Receiver (Facility), and the State Pollution Control Boards (of both the sender's and receiver's states in case of interstate transport).

q: Which form is used for filing the "Annual Return" by the hazardous waste generator to the State Pollution Control Board?
solution: Form 4: Used for filing the Annual Return regarding hazardous waste generation and management to the SPCB. It must be submitted by June 30th of the following financial year. Form 3: Used for maintaining daily records of hazardous waste operations. Form 10: Used for the Manifest system.

q: The toxicity of a hazardous waste is often measured using the "LD50" value. What does "LD50" signify?
options: Lethal Dose that kills 50% of the test population
solution: LD50 (Lethal Dose 50) is a standard measure of acute toxicity. It represents the amount of a substance (dose) required to kill 50% of a test population (usually laboratory animals like rats or mice) within a specified time. A lower LD50 indicates a more toxic substance.

q: In a "Secure Landfill" for hazardous waste, the double liner system typically consists of:
options: A primary HDPE geomembrane and a secondary compacted clay liner (or GCL)
solution: A Secure Landfill (designed for hazardous waste) requires a robust double liner system to prevent leachate from contaminating groundwater. This typically consists of: Primary Liner: A flexible geomembrane, usually High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) (typically 1.5 - 2.0 mm thick). Secondary Liner: A composite layer, often made of Compacted Clay Liner (CCL) or a Geosynthetic Clay Liner (GCL) with very low permeability.

q: Which process involves the addition of reagents to a liquid hazardous waste to produce a chemically stable solid product?
solution: Stabilization/Solidification is a chemical and physical process used to treat liquid or sludge hazardous wastes. Reagents (like cement, lime, or fly ash) are added to chemically bind the toxins ( Stabilization ) and convert the waste into a durable, solid block ( Solidification ), reducing the mobility of contaminants before landfill disposal. Vitrification turns waste into glass (too expensive for general use). Incineration is thermal destruction, not solidification.

q: Hazardous waste containing "Mercury" (e.g., thermometer waste) requires which specific treatment method?
solution: Mercury is a volatile heavy metal. Incineration is strictly prohibited for mercury-bearing waste because it releases toxic mercury vapors into the atmosphere. The standard treatment is Retorting , a thermal desorption process where the waste is heated in a closed system to vaporize the mercury, which is then condensed and recovered for recycling or safe disposal.

q: Under the Hazardous Waste Rules, "Schedule I" lists hazardous wastes based on:
options: List of waste to be imported
solution: The Hazardous Waste Rules classify waste into Schedules: Schedule I: Lists hazardous wastes generated by specific industrial processes (e.g., Petrochemicals, Tanning, Electroplating). Schedule II: Lists wastes based on concentration limits of hazardous constituents (Class A, B, and C).

q: "Leachate Collection System" is a mandatory component of:
solution: A Leachate Collection System is a critical engineering component of a Landfill . As rainwater percolates through waste, it becomes contaminated "leachate." This system (pipes and drainage layers at the bottom) collects the liquid to prevent it from leaking into the soil/groundwater and directs it to a treatment facility.

q: For the construction of a hazardous waste landfill, the bottom liner must have a permeability coefficient (k) less than:
solution: Purpose of the Liner: The primary function of a bottom liner in a landfill is to act as a barrier that prevents leachate (toxic liquid formed from waste) from percolating down and contaminating the soil and groundwater. Permeability Requirements: Hazardous Waste Landfills: Because hazardous waste poses a severe threat to health and the environment, the regulations are extremely strict. The bottom liner (usually a composite of clay and a geomembrane) must have a permeability coefficient (k) of less than or equal to cm/sec . This extremely low permeability ensures that any migration of contaminants is negligible over long periods. Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Landfills: For standard sanitary landfills dealing with non-hazardous municipal waste, the requirement is slightly less stringent, typically requiring a permeability of cm/sec .

q: Which of the following color codes is used for the "Manifest Copy" intended for the transporter?
solution: Under the color-coding scheme for the Manifest (Form 10) in the 2016 Rules: White: To SPCB (by Sender). Yellow: To SPCB (by Receiver). Pink: Retained by Receiver (Facility). Orange: Retained by Transporter. Green: Retained by Sender.

q: "Pantograph" or "Fingerprint Analysis" of hazardous waste is done to:
options: Identify the person who generated it
Verify the composition of waste against the declared parameters
Check the fingerprints of the driver
Measure the weight of the truck
solution: Fingerprint Analysis (or verification analysis) is a rapid screening test performed at the treatment, storage, and disposal facility (TSDF) when a waste shipment arrives. It ensures that the waste received matches the waste described in the manifest and the detailed laboratory analysis previously submitted by the generator, preventing the acceptance of unauthorized or incompatible wastes.

q: Which hazardous waste treatment method uses high-temperature oxidation to destroy organic contaminants?
solution: Incineration is the controlled burning of waste at high temperatures (typically ) in the presence of oxygen. It involves oxidation to break down organic contaminants into carbon dioxide, water, and ash, significantly reducing the volume and toxicity of the waste.

q: The "Rotterdam Convention" primarily deals with:
options: Prior Informed Consent (PIC) procedure for certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides
solution: The Rotterdam Convention is a multilateral treaty. Its main objective is to promote shared responsibility in the international trade of certain hazardous chemicals. It establishes the Prior Informed Consent (PIC) procedure, ensuring that importing countries know about the hazards of chemicals/pesticides before they agree to accept them. POPs relates to the Stockholm Convention . Ozone relates to the Montreal Protocol .
